_doc: Refugees (Systems/Refugees.cs): folk fleeing a struck settlement or a menace come up the road as travellers, camp free outside town and wait far longer than other travellers, longer still while homes and work are going up. A column of cardAt or more asks the mayor first (story refugee-column). They name the site that took their home and a plea (pleaBonus times a settlement's usual reward) stands to retake it while any wait in the camp. Sheltering them earns Mandate, their people's thanks and the town's haven fame; once the menace that drove them out falls, those not yet settled go home and rebuild.

draw._doc: How readily refugees pick this town over another: base, plus the best wall standing, plus the Mandate above 50 and the haven's fame, less its dread; the group's size is times this.

sources._doc: Folk who flee each kind of blow: least and most.

_tradesDoc: trades: what a people's refugees know (any profession buildings.json hires), for tradeShare of them; the rest are of the frontier's usual mix.

patience._doc: Days a refugee waits in the camp before taking the road on, a day more for each day homes or workplaces are going up, up to most; a day without rations costs one more.

welcome._doc: For each refugee taken in: Mandate and standing with every settlement of their people. Turned away: the same, lost.

home._doc: Once the menace that drove them out falls: refugees still in the camp go home, and a razed settlement they come from rises again at this prosperity, with this much more standing.

havens.title: a haven
havens.text: Word goes along the roads that {town} takes in those who have lost everything. People begin to call it a haven.

havens.title: the Refuge
havens.text: Forty families who fled their homes now call {town} theirs. In the villages they call it the Refuge, and they mean it kindly.

havens.title: the Shelter of the Realm
havens.text: A hundred souls who had nowhere else to go have found a home in {town}. Every road in the realm knows it now: the Shelter of the Realm turns no one away.

texts.home: {from} is safe again with {by} gone. {n} of its folk strike their tents outside {town} and go home.
texts.lost: The refugees from {from} say it was {site} that took their home. They ask the town's companies to take it back.

texts.rebuilt: {from} rises from its ashes. Its folk who sheltered in {town} came home to rebuild it, and they remember who took them in.
texts.fever: A fever from the crowded refugee camp
texts.grumble: The refugee camp outside {town} is crowded and hungry, and the town grumbles about it.
